title: Protocol for purification of cells in their native state using reversible aptamer-antidote pairs
protocol: Verify that the aptamer can selectively stain cells expressing its receptor target in an antidote-reversible manner.
Immobilize biotinylated aptamers on streptavidin-coated magnetic beads.
Bind and magnetically pull down target cells from blood or other complex cell mixtures using the aptamer-bead conjugates.
Remove the supernatant containing non-target cells to separate bound target cells.
Wash the beads to remove remaining weakly-bound non-target cells and other particles.
Incubate with antidote to displace bound target cells from the aptamer-coated beads, resulting in a population of label-free target cells in the supernatant.
Incubate a solution of biotinylated aptamers with streptavidin-coated magnetic beads.
Allow the mixture to incubate for 15 minutes.
Pretreat the sample containing the target cell type with RBC Lysis Buffer if it is blood, or directly resuspend in blocking PBS+.
Incubate the pretreated sample at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Use a magnet to separate the target cells bound to aptamer-coated beads from the rest of the sample.
Repeatedly use the magnet to partition the target cell-coated aptamer-magnetic beads.
Vortex the vial of Dynabeads™ MyOne™ Streptavidin C1 beads for 30 seconds.
Transfer 12 μL of beads to a 1.5 mL tube.
Wash beads by adding 375 μL of 1× SB1T buffer.
Place the tube in the magnetic rack for 1–2 minutes to pellet the beads.
Remove the supernatant carefully using a pipette.
Resuspend beads in 120 μL of 1× SB1T buffer by pipetting up and down 3–5 times.
Place the tube on a magnet for 1–2 minutes to pull out the beads.
Repeat steps b, c, and d two more times.
Aspirate the supernatant with a pipette after repeating the steps.
Resuspend the beads in 48 μL of 1× SB1T buffer + 1 mg/mL ssDNA.
Vortex to mix the targeting aptamer solution by resuspending 12.5 pmol of aptamer in 20 μL PBS+/+.
Heat the aptamer solution at 65°C for 5 minutes to denature it.
Allow the denatured aptamer to renature and fold at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Vortex the bead solution for at least 30 seconds.
Add 40 μL of the bead solution to the renatured aptamer solution from step 5.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature with gentle rotation for 15 minutes.
Place tubes on a magnet for 2–3 minutes to separate beads and supernatant.
Remove the supernatant gently using a pipette without aspirating any beads.
Wash the aptamer-coated beads three times.
Resuspend the beads with 50 μL 1× SB1 buffer + 1 mg/mL ssDNA.
Place the tube on the magnet for 2–3 min until the beads have been pulled out of solution.
Remove the supernatant gently with a pipette.
Repeat steps a, b, c, and d two more times.
Resuspend in buffer after removing the tube from the magnet following the third wash.
Resuspend beads in 40 μL of PBS+.
Place beads on ice until it is time to incubate with cell sample of interest.
Draw at least 1 mL of whole blood into a citrated collection tube to prevent clumping.
Combine 10 mL of 1× RBC Lysis Buffer with 1 mL of the citrated whole blood in a 15 mL conical and mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down 3–5 times.
Incubate the sample for 15 min at room temperature in a sample rotator.
Centrifuge the sample at 300–400 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove supernatant with a pipette, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.
Wash cells by resuspending in 10 mL PBS+.
Centrifuge at 300–400 × g for 5 min to pellet and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL PBS+ and keep on ice.
Immobilize aptamer-beads on the magnetic rack, remove supernatant, and replace with cell mixture.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Leave at 4°C for 30 min with gentle rotation to allow target cells to bind to aptamer-beads.
Place cell and bead mixture on the magnetic rack for 3–5 min to pellet the beads.
Remove supernatant gently using a pipette.
Resuspend cell-bead mixture in Media+ or PBS+.
Place the tube on a magnet for 3–5 minutes to pellet the beads.
Remove the supernatant to a second tube.
Place the second tube on a magnet for 3–5 minutes.
Transfer any residual supernatant from the second tube to a third tube.
Place the third tube on a magnet for 3–5 minutes.
Repeat the washing process as needed until no beads are visible in the supernatant.
Wash the cell-bead mixture twice more by repeating steps 2, 3, and 4.
Combine all bead-containing tubes after the final wash into a single tube.
Add a 100-fold molar excess of antidote to achieve a total volume of 40 μL.
Mix gently without forming bubbles.
Incubate at 37°C with gentle rotation for 10 minutes.
Place cells back at 4°C following antidote incubation.
Add 1 mL of Media+ or PBS+ buffer, mix by pipetting up and down.
Place tube on magnet for 3–5 minutes to draw beads out of solution.
Gently aspirate the supernatant containing detached target cells with a pipette.
Transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube.
Place the tube containing the supernatant on the magnet for 3–5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a second tube.
Repeat steps until no beads remain in the supernatant.
Discard tubes with residual beads.
Wash original beads two more times with 1 mL of PBS+ using described technique.
Pool supernatants from all washes and elution steps into Eppendorf tubes.
Spin tubes containing pooled eluted cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Gently remove the supernatant from the pellets of purified target cells.
Resuspend cell pellets in Media+ or other desired buffer.
Assess recovery by flow cytometry.
Stain a portion of the recovered cells with Hoechst 33342 to assess viability.
Prepare a solution of 1 ng/mL Hoechst 33342 staining solution in Hanks Balanced Salt Solution containing 1.3 mM Ca2+, 0.9 mM Mg2+, 1% BSA, and 0.1% sodium azide.
Alternatively, use commercially available viability dyes such as Zombie dyes from BioLegend™ according to the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Stain cells with biomarker-specific antibodies or biotinylated aptamers for target biomarker assessment.
Perform antibody staining for biomarkers following the manufacturer's guidelines immediately after "cell binding and antidote treatment".
Conduct aptamer staining for biomarker evaluation as described in the “aptamer cell staining assay” section.
Resuspend cells eluted from the beads in cell binding and antidote treatment in 100 μL of the Hoescht staining solution.
Assess sample purity and viability via flow cytometry, according to manufacturer specifications.
Prepare a dead cell control by incubating for 2 min in a solution of 70% ethanol in water.
